previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a male with a history of mixed Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma involving the central nervous system and eyes, was admitted for his eleventh cycle of high-dose methotrexate and rituximab chemotherapy. He presented in stable condition without new neurological or systemic symptoms. He received rituximab with premedication followed by high-dose methotrexate, with hydration, urinary alkalinization, and leucovorin rescue. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately, reaching 0.10 µM at discharge. A brain MRI showed no evidence of lymphoma recurrence, with stable non-enhancing lesions. He developed a mild, transient transaminitis that improved during the hospitalization. Due to the need to ensure safe methotrexate clearance and liver enzyme normalization, his stay was extended by one day. He was discharged home in stable condition on aspirin and omeprazole twice daily, with follow-up scheduled in two weeks.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ is a ___ right-handed man with CNS 
non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, as well as a history of systemic mixed 
Hodgkin's disease and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, who is here for IV 
rituximab and IV high-dose methotrexate therapy.  

(1) CNS Lymphoma:  Patient was treated with IV rituximab, 
high-dose methtorexate followed by leucovorin rescue.  He 
received aggressive fluids with sodium bicarbonate urine 
alkalinization.  Serum creatinine was followed for potential 
toxicity.  Patient had elevated transaminitis likely secondary 
to chemo, that trended down on discharge.  Prior to discharge 
patient also had MRI head that was stable.  Patient received 
seasonal flu vaccine on this admission.  On discharge 
methotrexate level was less than 0.04 uM.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  MR head without contrast.

HISTORY:  ___ male with CNS lymphoma, to evaluate for disease
response.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar MRI of the brain was performed without intravenous
contrast administration.

COMPARISON:  MRI brain ___.

FINDINGS:

There has been no significant interval change in size or appearance of the
FLAIR signal hyperintensity in the left posterior centrum semiovale
demonstrated on image 18, series 6.  Two additional punctate foci of FLAIR
signal hyperintensity are identified in the bilateral frontal lobes on series
6, image 20, unchanged from the previous examination.  While images are
degraded by motion artifact, no obvious new foci of FLAIR signal
hyperintensity are identified.  Gray-white matter differentiation is otherwise
preserved throughout.  The ventricles and cortical sulci are normal in size
and configuration without evidence of mass effect or shift of the normally
midline structures.  There is no evidence of restricted diffusion to suggest
acute ischemia.  The intracranial arterial flow voids are patent.  The
paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are well aerated.

IMPRESSION:

1. Stable examination with respect to at least three foci of FLAIR signal
hyperintensity as described above when compared with the previous examination
of ___.  No new FLAIR signal hyperintense foci are identified.  No acute
intracranial process identified.

INDICATION:  ___ man with CNS lymphoma.  Assess disease response.

COMPARISON:  Multiple head MRIs, most recent of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Please note that non-contrast head MRI was performed one day
prior.  Today only axial gradient echo and axial T1 post-contrast and sagittal
MP-RAGE images were obtained.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted images were
also displayed.

FINDINGS:  Again on the gradient echo sequence, there is an area of small
susceptibility artifact at the prior site of biopsy likely due to old blood
products or calcification, unchanged.  A small area of hyperintensity is noted
on the gradient echo sequence adjacent to this area of susceptibility
artifact, corresponding with a small FLAIR hyperintensity focus in the left
frontal lobe that was seen on the study performed the day before.  There are
no areas of abnormal enhancement.  The ventricles and sulci are normal in size
and configuration.  Major vascular flow voids are maintained.

IMPRESSION:  No areas of abnormal enhancement.  No significant change in
gradient echo and post-contrast sequences when compared to previous study of
___.

Follow up as clinically indicated.
